question.leadin: This country distanced itself from the Soviet Union during the Informbiro Period.
question.text: Name this country that broke up in 1992. It was led from 1953 to 1980 by Josip Tito, who led its resistance to fascism during the Second World War.
question.clue: After the second meeting of the Cominform in 1948, this country split with the Soviet Union.

swap.text: This Yugoslav Communist leader served as President from 1953-1980 and was one of the founders of the Non-Aligned Movement in 1961.
swap.clue: Fitzroy Maclean was this man's British liaison, and this ruler fought against the Ustasha and his nemesis Draza Mihailovic, leader of the Nazi-collaborationist Chetnik movement.

question.leadin: A "Big" version of this state, first ruled by Alexander of Battenberg, was proposed at the Treaty of San Stefano.
question.text: Name this country which experienced its namesake "Horrors" during an 1876 revolt against the Ottoman Empire. This country was united with Eastern Rumelia in 1885.
question.clue: One leader of this nation was ousted after members of the NGO Ecoglasnost were beaten by the police, leading to the one-year term of Petar Mladenov.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about tributaries of the Danube.
swap.text: The Prut River flows into the Danube after forming the border between Moldova and this country to its southwest, which has its capital at Bucharest.
swap.clue: Gaining independence after the Russo-Turkish War of 1878 under King Carol I, this country saw one long-time ruler begin a small cultural revolution with the July Theses and establish a police force called the Securitate.

question.text: The Ottomans fought this battle under the command of Murad I against the Serbs under Lazar. While both armies were wiped out, it led to a scarcity of Serbian troops, giving way to Serbian-Ottoman vassalage.
question.clue: Another source congratulates King Tvrtko I for success at this battle, which occurred on St. Vitus Day.

swap.leadin: His most famous action led to the July Crisis.
swap.text: Name this Serbian assassin who fatally shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand and thus helped cause World War I.
swap.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

question.leadin: This country's national hero, Skanderbeg ("SKAN-der-beg"), led the League of Lezhe ("LEH-zhuh") against the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: Name this country which was annexed by Italy during World War II. A communist dictator of this country, Enver Hoxha ("HOH-jah"), ordered the construction of thousands of bunkers.
question.clue: Its port-city of Vlore was the site of its proclamation of independence, as well as the site of major riots after this country's economy collapsed from a gigantic system of Ponzi schemes.

swap.text: Much of the ethnic strife of the 90s dates back to the atrocities of this Croatian ultranationalist organization formed by Ante Pavelic that cooperated with the Nazis in WWII.
swap.clue: This group of terrorists whose slogan "Za dom Spremni" means "Ready for the Fatherland."

question.leadin: This man was rumored to have banned the word "Dracula" in his country after he was taunted with that name on a 1978 visit to the United States.
question.text: Name this leader who promoted protochronism, which absurdly claimed that his country originated various cultural accomplishments attributed to others. This author of the July Theses was kept in power through a secret police known as the Securitate (seh-koo-rih-TAH-tay).
question.clue: He originally came to power after the death of Gheorgiu-Dej, and is also notable for staying out of the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia.

swap.leadin: A leader of these people left an army and used a forged letter to take over Kruje ("CREW-huh").
swap.text: Name these people who unified in the League of Lezhe ("leh-ZHUH"). The Treaty of Gaeta ended a revolt of these people led by the folk hero Skanderbeg.
swap.clue: A fighter for these people named George Kastrioti took a title meaning "Lord Alexander" in Turkish; that national hero was Skanderbeg.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a 1204 swerve that really surprised Byzantine-era observers.
question.text: An early event in the Fourth Crusade featured crusaders attacking this rival of Venice in November 1202. Pope Innocent III pointed out this city was a Catholic city and excommunicated the crusaders for going rogue.

swap.leadin: This state emerged as an independent polity after its first ruler Basarab won the Battle of Posada.
swap.text: Name this state, which later defended its independence from the Ottoman Empire at the Battle of Rovine under its ruler Mircea ("MEERCH-ya") the Great.

question.leadin: Besides Germany, this country contributed the most troops to the fascist invasion of the USSR.
question.text: Name this country, which lost Bessarabia and North Bukovina in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and then regained those territories in Operation Barbarossa. This country's Conducator overthrew its king Carol II.
question.clue: Though briefly restored by King Michael's Coup, this country's monarchy was abolished and replaced by the Iron Guard in 1940.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the hit Serbian propaganda song "God is a Serb," sometimes erroneously called "Serbia Strong."
swap.text: "God is a Serb" refers to Croats as members of this fascist organization. Founded by Ante Pavelic, it collaborated with German and Italian occupiers and nominally ruled Croatia during World War II.
swap.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

question.leadin: As the Nazis swept through Europe, many puppet states sprang up in various occupied territories.
question.text: A puppet state in this modern-day country was led by the Poglavnik Ante Pavelic inside of Nazi-occupied Yugoslavia.
question.clue: The Duke of Aosta was appointed as the monarch of this country under the name (+) Tomislav II despite never setting foot in this country.

swap.text: This country was once a part of Serbia. Slobodon Milosevic invaded this area in 1999, causing NATO to launch a retaliatory airstrike.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.text: Slobodan Milosevic's ("mee-lo-SHEV-eech's") Gazimestan Speech was on Kosovo's 600th anniversary, a national holiday named for this saint on whose day the battle occurred. A historical "dancing mania" was often named for either John or this saint.
question.answerHtml: Saint Vitus [or Vito; accept Guy or Guido; accept Saint Vitus Dance or El vito; accept Vidovdan]

swap.leadin: This man helped put down a peasant revolt in Galati in 1907, and once in power executed high level dignitaries at Jilava Prison.
swap.text: Identify this prime minister under King Carol II who allied his country with the Nazis during World War II.

question.leadin: Answer three questions about a fifteenth-century Balkan warrior.
question.text: This Albanian national hero defeated the armies of Sultans Murad II and Mehmet the Conqueror at two sieges of Croia, and he also defeated Venice, giving him the fortress of Dagnum.
question.clue: Pope Calixtus II chose this man to be Captain General of the Holy See in 1457.

swap.leadin: After this man was diagnosed with polycythemia, he joked that he was "suffering from an excess of reds."
swap.text: What Archbishop was controversially put on trial by Tito and convicted for treason for his relationship with the Ustase government during World War II? While eventually released from prison, he died soon after and was declared a martyr years later by Pope John Paul II.
